description: Product-policy classification of every original frontend conceptual state/feature for the modern product layer. Applies the PROJECT-PLAN.md modernization/subtraction rule: presentation artifacts and gameplay mechanics are preserved; administrative or hardware-era systems may be redesigned in Modern mode. Authentic/reference mode always reproduces stock behavior for every feature listed here. This file records product decisions and open questions; it is not fidelity evidence and never overrides analysis/ui-state-map.yml or analysis/ui-transition-contract.json.
authentic_mode_invariant: Every feature is reproduced as stock behavior in Authentic/reference mode. A Modern-mode disposition never authorizes guest WRAM/SRAM/simulation changes; redesigns attach through host/product interfaces (docs/MODERN-PRODUCT-LAYER.md).

classes.presentation_artifact: Player-visible communication: menu art, motion, typography, palette, icons, sounds, result rituals, indicators, secrets/discovery affordances. Preserve by default; elaboration may be added alongside.
classes.gameplay_mechanic: Rules that change what the player does or achieves: race simulation, scoring, medal thresholds, unlock conditions, mode rules. Preserve unless an evidence-backed product decision record exists.
classes.administrative: Systems whose main purpose came from shared-cartridge saves, limited storage, 1994 menu/controller conventions or content-padding repetition. Eligible for Modern-mode redesign or removal.

dispositions.preserve: Modern mode keeps the original feature unchanged.
dispositions.preserve_and_augment: Modern mode keeps the original feature and adds clearer information, conveniences or host input alongside it.
dispositions.redesign_decided: Product policy already decided to redesign this administrative feature in Modern mode; implementation is pending. Requires policy_source.
dispositions.redesign_candidate: Administrative feature eligible for Modern-mode redesign; the decision is open. Requires decision_gate.

features.rationale: Startup and splash are original presentation with their own skip affordance; nothing about them is hardware-era administration.

Modern preserves the original attract/demo cycle by default. A future Local Showcase using strong local completed runs may be offered only as an explicit optional attract mode; it does not silently replace the stock presentation artifact.

The tour reward scenes (medal scene, eight per-tour gold vignettes) and the ending (newspaper pages, WHODUNNIT credits, for Hunter gold) are reward presentations, and the Up-Left-Up-R-A splash cheat (all tours for one power-on, marked by the CHEAT! front page) is a stock secret; both stay intentionally opaque (R-2026-10-04-UI-22). The public Down+L+R+B chord does not exist as described.

Arrow cursor, menu art, motion, typography, palette and sounds are the recognizable menu character. Choices and grouping may change; the visual grammar may not be casually replaced. The decoded contract for typography, layout, cursor and slide transitions is analysis/generated/menu-visual-language.json.
A/B forward, X/Y back and D-pad cursor are the documented interaction character. Modern mode adds host keyboard support and rebinding without changing the guest-visible convention.

Modern uses task-oriented top-level navigation: Play, Practice, Multiplayer, Records, Options. Profile identity is handled above/beside this hub rather than hidden in Options. Authentic/reference mode retains the stock five-entry structure.

Every named/color-coded unicycle remains an exact selectable preset. Modern does not invent new canonical personalities for the 16 classic racers. Bronsen, Silvia, Goldwyn and ANTI-UNI remain the canonical stock opponent identities; recorded ghosts reflect the profile/racer that produced them. Optional later CPU/tournament reuse is content reuse, not new canon.
Named racers doubling as shared-cartridge save/profile slots is a storage-era constraint. Modern profiles separate save storage from racer identity.

Modern local multiplayer uses simultaneous independent join/racer selection. Shared-selector sequencing and claimed-rider exclusion are cartridge-era administration, not gameplay rules. Authentic/reference mode preserves the stock sequential handoff. Modern may allow duplicate classic presets, with player/viewport identity providing disambiguation.

PICK CHALLENGER appears only after a decided VS race and is driven by the loser's pad; the challenger then chooses the next track (five options); draws rematch automatically. This winner-stays contest structure is a mode rule. Reproduced on snesref (R-2026-10-03-UI-10); native/Mesen confirmation pending.
Animal tour icons and track-type icons are original indicators. Modern mode may add recent-track, practice and PB/medal information alongside.
Tour availability and the hidden Hunter tour are progression rules and a discovery reward. Unlock transition evidence is still open (UIQ-010).
Per-track medal thresholds define achievement. Modern mode shows exact target/medal deltas beside the original indicators; thresholds themselves are canonical in analysis/data/progression-model.json.

Modern removes mandatory Bronze→Silver→Gold re-clears. The player selects a challenge tier; completing a higher tier satisfies lower tiers. Canonical thresholds and Bronsen/Silvia/Goldwyn opponent identities remain authoritative. Authentic/reference mode preserves sequential stock progression.

Modern autosaves and resumes unfinished tours per profile. The current tour, completed events and selected racer/profile survive process exit and rider re-entry. Explicit Resume Tour and Restart Tour actions replace stock accidental loss; Authentic/reference mode retains stock behavior.
The sliding NOW PLAYING matchup card and RACE/EXIT choice are original race-entry ritual; modern mode may add rematch/next-event shortcuts around it.
Authoritative race simulation, timers, stunt scoring and AI are never altered by product policy.
Original HUD indicators stay; exact timing, splits and PB deltas are shown in addition.

The stock RACE/timer/CONTINUE GAME/QUIT overlay stays guest-owned. The modern host pause menu (Resume, Restart, Options, Controls, Run Data, Quit) is a separate host overlay that never writes guest memory or reinterprets stock pause state.
Result screens, score tallies and summing animations are original result rituals. Modern PB/medal deltas, Retry and records links are added alongside.

Modern preserves the stock result ritual, then offers contextual Next Event, Retry, Track Select, Tour Select and Records actions. Tour play emphasizes Next Event; Practice emphasizes Retry. This extends the stock VS navigation vocabulary rather than inventing a separate interaction language.
League standings and group tables are original score presentations; keep them reproducible as views even if League administration changes.

Modern replaces persistent cartridge-era multi-league administration with a Local Tournament setup flow: participants, event/track pool and format, with an active tournament persisted automatically. Round-robin/points league is the default format and original League standings remain available as a presentation view. Authentic/reference mode retains stock League.
Left+A+L+R erase-all and SELECT+Y+A league redefinition become explicit, confirmed UI actions in Modern mode.

Modern Options is settings-only: Video, Audio, Controls, Accessibility and Gameplay/Convenience. Records and profile administration live on their own product surfaces. Authentic/reference mode keeps the original Options grouping.

Modern provides one Records browser with Tracks, Racers/Profiles, Runs/Replays and Multiplayer/Tournament views. Original record tables remain available as Classic Tables or embedded views. Track pages may combine stock records, PB/previous run, medal targets, ghost selection and replay launch.
Gold/Silver/Bronze record tables, player-color star markers and score layouts stay as original views inside any modern records browser.
The WHAT IS YOUR PLAYER CALLED screen and alphabet grid are original presentation.

Modern uses native keyboard text entry plus a controller-friendly on-screen keyboard. Host profile/racer names may exceed stock field limits; when a guest-compatible name is required, derive a deterministic compatible alias/truncation. Authentic/reference mode preserves the stock alphabet grid.

Modern mode accepts forbidden names: the stock detection rule (71-word table at 83:85C5, case-insensitive substring match by 83:84DD; analysis/generated/forbidden-name-table.json) triggers a COOL NAME! acknowledgement and then the name is kept. Stock shows an inline NOT COOL ENOUGH message and keeps the editor open (analysis/generated/name-entry-probe.json); that rejection remains authentic/reference behavior only. The same stock check covers player and League names (one shared editor).
